lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Patricia, it's Rachel from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the cooking at home?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It didn't happen this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, if I plan it the night before, I can do it. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the cooking at home fit in your day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can cook on Sunday and have it for a few days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the cooking at home. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe cook at home 5 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 9. Maybe 10.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the cost gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the cost made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to cook at home 5 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Rachel. Bye!

flags.reason: Coach tells participant what the change is 'really about' without permission; imposes meaning rather than eliciting it.
Summary says 'the cost made this week harder'; participant never mentioned cost. Misattributes the barrier and may confuse the plan.
Participant says 'too tired for this right now'; coach jumps to praise in line 20 without exploring fatigue or the barrier.
'Once you decide something, you follow through' is not supported by the participant's account of repeated non-follow-through.

score.summary: Coach covered the full call structure and elicited several change statements, including the goal of cooking five nights and a backup walking plan. However, the coach praised past the participant's fatigue and sustain talk, offered some ungrounded affirmations, and misstated a barrier as 'cost' in the summary.
strengths: Line 31 complex reflection captures the participant's movement and desire to keep going.
Line 40 and 47 emphasize autonomy ('It's your plan', 'It's completely your call') and support participant choice.
Line 59 open question about a backup plan (barrier planning) led to a concrete walking alternative in line 60.
coaching_tips: Line 19: when the participant says 'too tired for this right now,' explore it with an open question before affirming.
Line 22 and 24: tie affirmations to specific things the participant said so they feel earned, not generic.
Line 53: ask permission or reflect the participant's own reasons instead of telling her what the change is about.
Line 61: check the summary against what was said; the participant never mentioned cost, so use her words (e.g., 'knees' or 'tiredness').
